title: registry.config.json
description: Repo-level settings for a bht-component-registry site. Everything here is non-secret and committed; secrets (publish and read tokens) live only in CI secrets or your shell.

scope.description: Your primary npm scope without the @, e.g. "acme" for @acme/*. Every component this registry generates is published under it. Must be lowercase, DNS-label safe, and not a reserved word. Create the matching org on npmjs before your first publish.

npmRegistry.description: Where PUBLIC packages publish and where the Changelog tab looks up their published versions. Default is npmjs; GitHub Packages is https://npm.pkg.github.com; a private registry is whatever URL it gives you.

privateRegistry.description: Where PRIVATE packages publish (a package the generator was told is private, or whose publishConfig says so): GitHub Packages, Verdaccio, Artifactory, a paid npmjs org, and the like. Leave it out and every package is public. A package never moves between the two after its first release; `pnpm check:publish` enforces that.

templateVersion.description: The bht-component-registry template version this repo was created from or last updated to. Maintained by `npx create-bht-component-registry update`; do not edit by hand.

site.description: Branding for the docs site. Code never needs to change for these.

title.description: Site name, shown in the header and the <title>.

url.description: Where the docs site is served, e.g. "https://components.acme.example". With it set, `pnpm release` gives each published package its docs page as `homepage` and a `Docs:` line in its README, so the npm page points here rather than at the repository.

description.description: One sentence for the home page hero and <meta name="description">.

logo.description: The header logo, shown instead of the title text. A file under branding/ at the repo root, e.g. "logo.svg" (served at /branding/logo.svg); an absolute URL also works. `update` never touches branding/.

logoDark.description: A logo for the dark scheme, swapped in automatically; omit to use `logo` in both. A file under branding/ at the repo root, e.g. "logo.svg" (served at /branding/logo.svg); an absolute URL also works. `update` never touches branding/.

favicon.description: The browser-tab icon (<link rel="icon">), ideally an SVG. Omit to keep the template's default favicon.ico. A file under branding/ at the repo root, e.g. "logo.svg" (served at /branding/logo.svg); an absolute URL also works. `update` never touches branding/.

icons.description: Larger icons for home screens and install prompts, as PNG files under branding/.

themeColor.description: <meta name="theme-color">: the browser-chrome tint on mobile. Defaults to theme.primary.

headerTheme.description: "dark" keeps the header on the dark scheme's surface in both colour schemes, so a light wordmark always has its background.

primaryColor.description: Older alias of theme.primary, kept so existing configs keep working. Prefer `theme`.

theme.description: Seed colours for the site's Material Design 3 theme. The build generates every colour role for the light and dark schemes from them with Google's material-color-utilities (the same algorithm as the Material Theme Builder) into src/generated/theme.css. The /theme page lets you pick these interactively and download the same CSS for your own app.

primary.description: The primary seed: the brand colour. MD3 picks the tone that reads; a very dark or very light brand colour still yields a legible primary.

secondary.description: A pinned secondary seed (keeps its own hue and chroma). Omit and MD3 derives a muted secondary from the primary.

tertiary.description: A pinned tertiary seed. Omit and MD3 derives one by hue rotation.

neutral.description: A neutral seed: backgrounds and surfaces take its hue at MD3's low chroma. Omit and they follow the primary.

scheme.description: The MD3 scheme variant. tonalspot is Material's default; fidelity and content keep the primary closest to the seed; neutral and monochrome desaturate.

overrides.description: Hand edits to single roles after generation, per scheme. The /theme page writes this for you when you edit a swatch.

light.description: Role name in camel case as material-color-utilities names it ("primary", "onPrimaryContainer") to a hex colour.

dark.description: Role name in camel case as material-color-utilities names it ("primary", "onPrimaryContainer") to a hex colour.

fonts.description: Self-hosted web fonts from branding/fonts, loaded with next/font/local (no request to a font service at build or run time). Omit a slot to keep Inter, the template's default. Latin woff2 files for most open fonts are in the @fontsource packages on npm.

path.description: A font file under branding/, e.g. "fonts/ubuntu-latin-400.woff2".

weight.description: CSS font-weight the file covers: "400", "700", or a range like "100 900" for a variable font.

body.description: The body face: body, label and title roles.

path.description: A font file under branding/, e.g. "fonts/ubuntu-latin-400.woff2".

weight.description: CSS font-weight the file covers: "400", "700", or a range like "100 900" for a variable font.

heading.description: The heading face: headline and display roles. Omit to use the body face.

hero.description: The home page hero. Defaults: the site title and description, a "Browse components" button into your scope and, when the Docs section has pages, a "Docs" button.

actions.description: Replaces the default buttons entirely. The first is primary unless `variant` says otherwise.

embedDesigns.description: Show a component's Figma links as embedded frames on its Design tab. Off by default: an embed is a third-party iframe and the Figma file must be visible to whoever views the site. Other design links are always shown as cards.

design.description: The design-system file — a Figma URL or any URL — linked from the design-tokens page. A string, or { label, url }.

docs.description: Behaviour of the docs site, as opposed to `site`, which is branding. Every key has a default; the object may be omitted.

history.description: Docs for earlier versions of each component. `pnpm version-packages` snapshots a component's README, source, examples and props into docs-history/<scope>/<category>/<name>/<version>/ (committed with the version bump), and the site builds a page per version with a switcher on the component page.

enabled.description: false: no snapshots are written and no version pages are built.

keep.description: Which snapshots to keep per component: "all"; a number, the newest N; or "majors", the newest of each older major plus everything in the current major. Pruned folders stay in git history.

themeBuilder.description: Build the /theme page: pick seed colours, see every MD3 role update, edit roles, and download the CSS or the site.theme snippet.
